Subject: SEV-1: inference cluster outage (prod-west1)

Team —

Automated monitor: prod-west1 inference cluster is returning 502s for model shards backing long-running streaming sessions. Error rate has crossed SEV-1 threshold for BrightLeaf tenant (region us-west1). Impact: inference requests are failing or timing out for BrightLeaf production traffic.

What we know so far:
- Start time: ~2026-07-15T08:53 PDT
- Symptoms: KV cache desync + kernel misallocation resulting in partial model load failures (502/503).
- Affected customers: BrightLeaf (high traffic), two small internal test tenants.

Immediate asks:
- Marcus: please join bridge and surface any model-side changes or recent kernel rollouts (suspect kernel selector mismatch).
- Monica: please loop in the BrightLeaf CSM and prepare an executive-facing note (I can send).
- Vivek/Evelyn: please prepare to coordinate credits/SLAs if this persists.

Bridge (established): Zoom + redwood bridge pinned — https://zoom.us/j/9876543210?pwd=sev1bridge (host: dylan.brooks)
Logs attached: sev1-logs.txt (tail + error traces).

I will update every 15 minutes or on any material change.

—Dylan

Subject: Redwood Inference — Executive update: service disruption affecting BrightLeaf (Jul 15)

Samantha / BrightLeaf ops team —

First, I want to apologize for the disruption you are seeing this morning. We have declared a SEV-1 event affecting inference traffic for BrightLeaf in the us-west region. This note summarizes what we know, what we are doing now, and next steps. I will keep you updated on a 30-minute cadence or sooner for material changes.

Summary of impact
- Start: ~2026-07-15T08:53 PDT
- Scope: BrightLeaf production inference requests intermittently fail (502/503) or experience high latency; non-streaming batch jobs are degraded but still progressing for some workloads.
- Customers impacted: BrightLeaf production cluster (primary); a small subset of internal test traffic.

What we are doing right now
- Engineering has opened a dedicated bridge and is actively investigating kernel allocator behavior and KV cache desynchronization for the prod-west1 model shards.
- Mitigation in progress: rolling fallback to compatible model-variant nodes (can accept traffic within 10–15 minutes per shard), and selective restart of affected serving processes to rebuild KV caches.
- Estimated mitigation ETA (best effort): 30–45 minutes to restore majority of traffic; full recovery may take longer depending on shard rebuild times.

Customer-facing actions we will take
- We will prioritize BrightLeaf traffic across the fleet and restrict non-critical background rebuilds until your traffic stabilizes.
- We will prepare a post-incident report within 72 hours and share a draft for your review.
- If the impact extends beyond 2 hours, we will propose a commercial credit consistent with our SLA and discuss tailored remediation.

Contact points on the bridge
- Engineering lead: Dylan Brooks (dylan.brooks@redwood.com)
- Solutions/technical lead: Marcus Lin (marcus.lin@redwood.com)
- CSM: Monica Patel (monica.patel@redwood.com)
- Executive contact: Evelyn Hart (evelyn.hart@redwood.com)

Attachments: redwood-exec-update.pdf (one-page summary)
Bridge link: https://zoom.us/j/9876543210?pwd=sev1bridge

We take incidents like this very seriously and will be as transparent as possible while the team corrects course. Please reply to this thread or join the bridge if you want live updates.

Sincerely,

Date: 2026-07-16T10:12:05-07:00
Subject: Post-incident: draft postmortem & customer review timeline

Folks —

Following yesterday’s SEV-1, engineering has confirmed the root cause as a combination of a kernel selector regression deployed to prod-west1 and an associated KV cache mismatch triggered by a rolling restart window. The immediate mitigations (rollback of selector, selective process restarts, and prioritized traffic routing) recovered 95% of BrightLeaf traffic by 10:00 PDT on Jul 15; we continued background shard rebuilds overnight.

I’ve attached a first-draft postmortem and a CSV timeline for internal review (postmortem-draft.md, timeline.csv). Proposed public cadence:
- Draft shared with BrightLeaf within 24 hours for fact check (today).
- Final postmortem published within 72 hours (by 2026-07-18) with remediation plan & SLA credit assessment.

Action items:
- Monica: please send the draft to Samantha and Anil with a review deadline of 24 hours.
- Evelyn: coordinate exec-level note offering an SLA credit range if BrightLeaf confirms impact duration >2 hours.
- Dylan: include relevant logs and kernel selector diff in the postmortem appendix.

Let me know if anything else should be added before we share externally.

—Marcus
